flourish

/FLUR-ish/ — rhymes with nourish · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To flourish is to grow, develop, or thrive vigorously and successfully.

Tomatoes flourish in this sunny corner of the garden.

Example

After the rain, wildflowers flourished across the meadow, creating a spectacular carpet of color that spread for acres.

Flourish is more precise than 'grew' because it emphasizes not just growth but vigorous, successful growth. The wildflowers aren't just getting bigger—they're thriving in brilliant color and spreading widely, which is exactly what flourish captures.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

grow: Grow simply means to get bigger or develop over time, and it is neutral - weeds grow, problems grow, so does a child. Flourish claims much more: vigorous, healthy, successful growth that is plainly going well, not just an increase in size.

thrive: Thrive means doing very well and steadily improving - a thriving business, a thriving student. It names the healthy state itself. Flourish adds the visible display of that health: something that flourishes is not only doing well but showing it, spreading, blooming, unmistakably alive.

prosper: Prosper means to succeed, especially in money or material terms - a prospering shop turns a growing profit. Flourish is broader and more alive: gardens, friendships, and ideas flourish when they grow vigorously, whether or not any wealth is involved.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wilt: to droop and lose freshness or strength

decline: to grow steadily weaker, smaller, or worse

Where it sits · how vigorously it grows

wilt → survive → flourish → blossom

wilt vs. flourish: Wilt is the opposite end of the scale from flourish: a wilting plant droops and fades, while a flourishing one grows stronger every day.

survive vs. flourish: Survive is much weaker than flourish — surviving means merely staying alive, while flourishing means growing vigorously and succeeding.

blossom vs. flourish: Blossom is a notch stronger than flourish: flourishing means thriving steadily, while blossoming means bursting into full, spectacular bloom.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — flour: flower, bloom (from Latin flor-, 'flower,' via Old French floriss-; spelled flour- in this word)

Suffix — -ish: verb-forming ending (from French -iss-) (Old French)

Put it together: Flour ('flower, bloom' — the Latin root flor-, 'flower,' as it came to be spelled in this word via Old French) + -ish (verb-forming ending): to flourish is literally 'to flower' — to bloom, thrive, and grow vigorously and successfully.

Use the root in a new word: florist: On the morning of the wedding, the florist's van pulled up with the last of the arrangements.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Flourish is the word for vigorous, successful growth and development. Use it when something is not just alive but truly thriving and visibly developing. For slower or uncertain growth, or mere survival, 'grow' or 'survive' is more accurate.
